title: Opportunity cost is the value of the best forgone alternative
learning_objectives: Identify the best forgone alternative in a choice.
Include relevant non-monetary costs such as time.
Avoid adding the values of every possible alternative.

sources.title: How Individuals Make Choices Based on Their Budget Constraint

misconceptions.description: Opportunity cost is always equal to the money paid.
Opportunity cost is the sum of all alternatives not chosen.

critical_errors.description: Defines opportunity cost as only the explicit purchase price.
Adds mutually exclusive forgone alternatives instead of selecting the best one.

teaching_brief.goal: Help the learner identify the most valuable alternative sacrificed by a decision.
teaching_brief.learner_profile: A beginner who equates cost with cash expenditure.
instructions: Use one example involving money and one involving time.
Ask which single alternative would have been chosen next.
Distinguish sunk costs from the opportunity cost of the current decision.
Have the learner generate a personal low-stakes example.
prohibited_disclosures: Do not reveal held-out item wording.
Do not define opportunity cost as the sum of all rejected choices.

pretest.prompt: You spend a free evening at a concert instead of studying, your best alternative. What is the opportunity cost?

choices.text: Only the ticket price
The value of the study opportunity forgone, plus other relevant incremental resources
Every activity you could possibly imagine
Zero because the evening was free

pretest.prompt: Why is opportunity cost based on the best forgone alternative?

choices.text: Only one mutually exclusive alternative would actually have been selected next.
All alternatives can be consumed simultaneously.
Money is irrelevant to every decision.
The chosen option has no benefits.

posttest.prompt: A student takes an unpaid internship. The best alternative is a paid job. What belongs in the opportunity cost?

choices.text: The wages and other value forgone from the paid job
Only the internship's commuting cost
The income of every job in the city added together
Nothing because the internship is unpaid

posttest.prompt: A nonrefundable ticket was purchased last month. When deciding today whether to attend, which fact is most relevant?

choices.text: The ticket price must determine today's choice.
Compare today's benefits and costs, including the best use of the time; the sunk ticket payment cannot be recovered.
Opportunity cost no longer exists.
Add the value of every possible activity.

transfer.prompt: A lab uses its only microscope for Project A. Project B was the next-best feasible use. What is the microscope-related opportunity cost?

choices.text: The value Project B would have produced
The original purchase price only
The value of Projects B, C, D, and every future idea added together
Zero because the lab already owns it

transfer.prompt: A free online course requires 30 hours. What shows that it still has a cost?

choices.text: The 30 hours could have been used for the best alternative activity.
Free goods never require choices.
Only prices create scarcity.
Time has no economic value.

retention.prompt: Opportunity cost is best summarized as...

choices.text: the value of the next-best alternative forgone
the sum of all imagined alternatives
only explicit cash spending
a past payment that cannot change

retention.prompt: Which resource can create opportunity cost even when no money is paid?

choices.text: Time
Only coins
Only bank loans
None
